content.title: Venezuelan Bonds Rally on Maduro Ouster
content.summary: International debt issued by the Venezuelan government and state-owned oil company PdVSA rallied on Monday after the U.S. ouster of President Nicolás Maduro.  Investors are betting that the Trump administration's capture of Maduro will clear the way for a restructuring of Venezuela's sovereign debt, which the government defaulted on in 2017 after the U.S. imposed sanctions on the Maduro regime.  The sanctions have made it impossible for international investors who lent billions of dollars to Venezuela to negotiate a restructuring.

content.title: Treasury Yields Set to End the Year Lower After Fed Rate Cuts
content.summary: U.S. Treasury yields are set to end the year lower after the Federal Reserve cut interest rates three times in the second half of the year, with further reductions expected during 2026.  Yields had jumped higher in the first half of 2025 after President Trump's announcement of hefty trade tariffs in April sparked concerns about long-term inflationary and economic pressures.  Ten-year Treasury yields last trade down 1.8 basis points at 4.112%, having started 2025 at 4.571%, Tradeweb data show.

content.title: Treasury Yields Steady After Rising Following Strong GDP Data
content.summary: Treasury yields were steady in thin trade on a holiday-shortened week, reversing much of Tuesday's rise after data showed the U.S. economy grew at a 4.3% annual pace in the third quarter.  This lifted two-year Treasury yields to a 13-day high of 3.559% as investors trimmed expectations for another interest-rate cut in January.  The 10-year Treasury yield fell 0.8 basis point to 4.161%, having hit a 13-day high of 4.202% on Tuesday, Tradeweb data show.
